IO is slower than Base with substantial recorded HOL cycles; OO records retire/reclaim activity and a lower terminal cycle count. No unmeasured average-live-miss quantity is inferred.
The IO row is slower than Base and has the largest recorded HOL-cycle scale; the OO row records retire/reclaim counters and improves over IO. Classification is limited to those source metrics.

The measured modes reduce global-read and L1-miss traffic relative to Base while retaining zero L2 misses/reservation failures; this names a traffic contrast without assigning an unsupported micro-causal mechanism.

The accepted modes show a large L2-reservation-fail traffic contrast and the Base row has nonzero PIB/cacheline pressure; the traffic class is primary because the direct traffic field changes are retained.
